# An unsupported-construct message names what to change
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #353, sha256:bda6a1e8dd9ccc4465aa46529d6784b2ed787fa9ff327562c91153d4c565689f). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Draft
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** bug (found by the card 189 gate review and sign-off: some PH340 messages are vague or point at the wrong place)
- **Repository:** avowry (src/Avowry.Adapters.CSharp/CSharpProvider.cs, docs/GRAMMAR.md, tests/Avowry.Acceptance.Tests/UnsupportedCsharpConstructs.cs)
- **Source:** card 189's gate review and sign-off (2026-11-08): `the outcome 'returns of type Box' in spec 'rec' yet` is clumsy; the messages for a call argument, an effectful callee and a stored field do not name the argument, the callee or the field; the position of `more than one effect` is the avow, not the `effects` clause.
- **Depends on:** 189 (done)
- **Story:** As Ari, I want each "the C# target does not support X yet" message to name the thing I wrote and where it is, so that I rewrite it without guessing.
- **Consumer value:** Ari reads a message and rewrites the right construct in one attempt; we see it when each row's message names its argument, callee, field or clause.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Scenario: [O][M] each message names its thing
     Given the unsupported constructs of card 189
     When `avowry build` prints the diagnostic
     Then the message names the call argument, the callee, the stored field or the returned value kind that is unsupported
  2. Scenario: [B] the position is the construct's
     Given a composite with two effects
     When the diagnostic is printed
     Then its line and column are those of the `effects` clause
  3. Scenario: [I] the documented text matches
     Given the PH340 row of docs/GRAMMAR.md
     When it is compared with the messages
     Then the listed constructs are the ones the messages name
  Letters that do not apply: [Z] and [E] are covered by card 189's rows; [S] is the single-row case of criterion 1.
- **Not in this card:** supporting any of the constructs; new codes; the diagnostic column test (its own card).
- **Size:** S
